result.summary: Caches the serialized compact block message within an asynchronously launched shared future so it can be reused for both high-bandwidth announcements and low-bandwidth getdata responses. It groups the cached recent block state variables into a single struct, extracts compact block transmission logic into a shared SendCompactBlock helper, and hardens PeerHasHeader against null pointer dereferences.
result.problem: Compact block messages served to low-bandwidth peers via getdata are reconstructed and serialized per peer instead of reusing the cached message constructed during block reception. In addition, upcoming work to support compact block prefilling in PR 35558 risks duplicate serializations without structured message caching.
evidence: PR description: 'Performance is less critical for low-bandwidth peers, so this change on its own should have little impact on block propagation, but these refactors are useful as part of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35558 which adds prefilling of compact blocks, and where we run the risk of potentially having to serialize more than one cmpctblock_msg (one prefilled and one not-prefilled).'

Commit 42a992816a: 'This also changes std::launch::deferred to std::launch::async since we are likely going to use this result very soon if someone has requested HB blocks from us, and if no one has, then performance here is not that critical.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added a commit making PeerHasHeader take CNodeState by reference and asserting pindex is non-null.
result.card: Caches serialized compact block messages asynchronously to serve both high-bandwidth announcements and low-bandwidth getdata requests from the same cached message. It also consolidates recent block tracking state and unifies compact block dispatching logic. The author states that standalone propagation impact is minimal because low-bandwidth peers are not on the latency-critical path, but the refactor prepares the codebase for prefilled compact block relay in PR 35558. A flaw in compact block delivery logic could disrupt or delay block relay to peers.

risk.why: A flaw in compact block serialization or header tracking could corrupt block relay messages or stall block propagation to connected peers.
